messages.content: How do you build strength efficiently?

Progressive overload is the only principle that matters: consistently increase the stimulus (weight, reps, or density) over time. Frequency: each muscle group 2-3x/week produces more growth than 1x/week with same weekly volume. Compound movements (squat, deadlift, press, pull) deliver more per unit time than isolation exercises. Protein: 1.6-2.2g per kg bodyweight per day — the ceiling above which additional protein produces no additional muscle growth. Sleep: growth hormone released during deep sleep is the primary anabolic signal — training without adequate sleep produces significantly less adaptation. Consistency over 6-24 months produces results no supplement or optimisation protocol can match.
What does the science say about sleep optimisation?

Sleep is the highest-impact performance intervention available. During sleep: memory consolidation, metabolic waste clearance (glymphatic system), hormone regulation (testosterone, growth hormone primarily released during deep sleep), and emotional processing. Optimisation: consistent sleep and wake times (circadian rhythm is the primary regulator), cold dark room (temperature drop triggers sleep onset), no blue light 1-2 hours before sleep (suppresses melatonin), no caffeine after 12pm (8-hour half-life means 4pm coffee = two cups at midnight), no alcohol (fragments sleep architecture and suppresses REM). Sleep deprivation of 6 hours for 10 days produces cognitive impairment equivalent to 24 hours without sleep — and sufferers underestimate their impairment.
What does the evidence say about optimal nutrition for cognitive performance?

Cognitive performance is most affected by: glucose stability (spikes and crashes impair focus — complex carbohydrates and protein rather than sugar), hydration (even 1-2% dehydration measurably impairs cognitive function), omega-3 fatty acids (DHA is the structural component of brain cell membranes — oily fish 2-3x/week or algae-based supplement), and sleep quality (which is heavily influenced by diet — avoid large meals, alcohol, and caffeine in the 3-4 hours before sleep). The Mediterranean diet pattern has the strongest evidence base for cognitive health and dementia prevention. Fasting (16-18 hours) increases BDNF (brain-derived neurotrophic factor) — the primary driver of neuroplasticity.
